observations: Photo 0 shows a used inline four-cylinder petrol car engine sitting on the ground at a parts yard, with another engine behind it.
Four coil-on-plug ignition coils in the valve cover, a black plastic intake manifold, wiring loom, alternator and a ribbed drive belt pulley are fitted.
Green spray paint marks across the valve cover, coils and manifold, as dealers mark stock.
No maker badge, engine code, displacement or plate is readable in the photo; a faint watermark is unreadable.
Low-resolution single photo from above; block, sump, engine code stamp and gearbox side are not shown.
Engine is not running and not connected to anything in the photo.

claims.evidence: No maker logo or engine code is readable in photo 0.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo of the engine; no import papers shown.
No clip of the engine running on a test stand.
A loose engine has no odometer; mileage cannot be shown remotely.
Paint marks are visible in photo 0, but no close-up of head bolts, gasket seals or sump bolts.

risks.risk: Engine maker, code and size unknown, and they set the price.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine code stamped on the block and any label on the valve cover or manifold.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced until the engine code is read

risks.risk: Engine does not run, knocks, smokes or has low compression.
risks.proof: Clip of the engine starting and idling on a test stand, with sound, showing the exhaust.

risks.risk: Engine has been opened or rebuilt, or has cracks or oil leaks.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of head bolts, head gasket line, sump and both sides of the block.

risks.risk: Ancillaries missing (starter, sensors, injectors, throttle body).
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides of the engine showing every fitted part.
risks.if_unproven: as bare engine with only the parts visible in photo 0

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code stamped on the block.
Clip of the engine running on a test stand with sound.
Photos of all four sides of the engine and the underside.
Close-up of head bolts and gasket line to show it has not been opened.
response.reason: It is a used four-cylinder petrol engine, but no maker, engine code or size can be read in the only photo, and that is what sets the price. A photo of the stamped engine code is needed before even a worst case price is possible.
